STEP 1 - Scene: A snack of almonds on a square white plate, photographed from directly above.

STEP 2 - Ruler: The plate is a square-ish dish, about 20 cm along its longest width (diagonal about 22 cm). The effective area is about 20 x 20 = 400 cm² minus the rounded corners, so roughly 330 cm².

STEP 3 - Items: Whole raw or dry-roasted almonds only. There is no oil or sauce.

STEP 4 - Area: Counting about 30 almonds, each about 2.2 x 1.2 cm, which is about 2.2 cm² each, gives about 65 cm². That is roughly 20% of the plate, and it is the only food.

STEP 5 - Volume: The almonds are about 0.8 cm thick and mostly one layer, with a few overlapping in the cluster. Taking 65 cm² x 0.8 cm gives about 52 ml. Counting pieces instead, each almond is about 2.2 x 1.2 x 0.8 cm, which is about 1.5 ml per nut, so 30 nuts come to about 45 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: A single almond weighs about 1.2 g, so 30 almonds weigh about 36 g. The volume method gives 50 ml x 0.65 bulk density, which is about 33 g. I'll use about 35 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: Almonds have about 579 kcal per 100 g, so 35 g gives about 203 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: 30 almonds weigh about 35 g and carry about 200 kcal, which is plausible for a small handful.
